title: A methodology for measuring the form of organic settlements
author: Zeka, Yuzer

steps.title: Prepare vector data and layers
steps.instruction: Obtain vector‑format maps of the study area and open them in AutoCAD. Create five separate layers named: study area boundary, street lines, block lines, parcel lines, and building lines.

steps.title: Convert layers to polyline/polygon and export
steps.instruction: In AutoCAD convert each of the five layers to polyline (for lines) or polygon (for areas) format, then export each layer individually to ArcGIS and save them as shapefiles.

steps.title: Calculate surface areas in ArcGIS
steps.instruction: For each component (study area, streets, blocks, buildings) in ArcGIS: open the attribute table, choose Table Options → Add Field, set Name = surface, Type = Long Integer, click OK; right‑click the new surface column, select Calculate Geometry, set Property = Area, Units = meters (m) or hectares (ha), click OK. The area of the selected unit is then recorded.

steps.title: Export attribute tables to Excel
steps.instruction: Open the attribute table of a component, Table Options → Select All, right‑click → Copy Selected, open a new Excel worksheet and paste. Use the exported tables to obtain total counts (shown at the bottom of each table) and to compute ratios such as Plot Coverage Ratio = total building surface ÷ total block surface.

steps.title: Calculate street segment lengths
steps.instruction: In ArcGIS, select the street polyline layer, open its attribute table, Table Options → Add Field, set Name = Length, Type = Double, click OK; right‑click the Length column, Calculate Geometry, Property = Length, Units = meters (m) or kilometers (km), click OK. The length of each street segment is recorded.

steps.title: Measure street orientation and directional change
steps.instruction: In AutoCAD, for each street segment intersect it with a vertical (north‑south) line and a horizontal (east‑west) line; use the Angle command to obtain the segment’s orientation angle relative to the coordinate system. For directional change, select two adjacent street segments and apply the Angle command to obtain the angle between them. Record all angles in Excel and generate distribution charts.

steps.title: Measure street width and related parameters
steps.instruction: Across the settlement measure: (a) street width, (b) width‑to‑building‑height ratio, (c) width‑shift distance, and (d) width‑shift frequency. Perform these measurements in AutoCAD/ArcGIS at representative street edges, especially where building façades enclose the street. Export the numeric results to Excel for frequency and distance analysis.

steps.title: Analyze block pattern
steps.instruction: Calculate each block’s surface area in ArcGIS using the same field‑addition method as for streets. Export block areas to Excel to determine the most common, largest, and smallest block sizes. Determine block dimensions by measuring the longest length and width in two orthogonal directions (method analogous to street length measurement). Export block‑level data to compute: number of parcels per block, number of buildings per block, and block‑scale Plot Coverage Ratio (building surface ÷ block surface). Summarize minimum, maximum, and modal values in Excel.

steps.title: Measure parcel pattern
steps.instruction: Compute parcel surface areas in ArcGIS and export to Excel for min, max, and modal parcel size. In AutoCAD measure each parcel’s width and depth, categorize widths and depths into intervals, and import the interval counts into Excel. Calculate width‑to‑depth proportions and produce charts. Classify each parcel’s position relative to the street into four categories: narrow side, long side, quadrate parcel, and corner parcel; count occurrences and record in Excel.

steps.title: Assess building location and orientation
steps.instruction: Categorize every building according to its position on the parcel (e.g., front yard only, back yard only, side yard combinations, courtyard, no yard) using the matrix shown in Table 2 (e.g., F, B, 1S, 2S, F1S, F2S, B1S, B2S, FB1S, FB2S, NY). Also record the building’s front‑façade orientation using compass points (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW). Export the classifications to Excel to determine the most common orientation and yard configuration.

steps.title: Calculate building setbacks and façade ratios
steps.instruction: For each parcel, measure the average setback distance from the building to each parcel border side; record all setback values in Excel and categorize them (e.g., 0‑2 m, 2‑5 m, >5 m). Identify buildings whose façades lie on the street edge, compute the proportion of building façade length versus void (open) space along the street elevation, and analyse the rhythm of height change along the street façade. Export all results to Excel for statistical summarisation.
